_comment: Invalidation correctness scenarios, hand-authored ground truth. Each scenario names memories that SHOULD be invalidated (targetMemories) by the given trigger, and 'bystander' memories that share a substring/token/topic with the trigger but MUST NOT be invalidated. Mirrors hippo-memory's own 'BYSTANDER LOCK' regression-test class (see benchmarks/README.md). Scenarios 1-4 exercise rAIminiscence's v9 Commit Invalidation (a memory with no relatedFiles, staled when its body mentions the outgoing target of a qualifying commit-subject shape: migrate/switch/move/convert/transition/upgrade ... from X to Y, replace X with Y, deprecate X, remove/drop X). Scenario 5 exercises rAIminiscence's v2 file-based invalidation instead (a memory anchored via relatedFiles, staled when git shows one of those files changed after the memory's createdAt). For hippo-memory, every scenario is driven via its own single invalidation primitive, `hippo invalidate "<pattern>"` (content-overlap matching) — see benchmarks/README.md's mapping-compromise note on why scenario 5's file-anchoring semantics can't be reproduced faithfully in hippo-memory.

scenarios.description: A commit moving the build off webpack should invalidate memories describing webpack usage, without touching unrelated memories that merely share the 'web' prefix.
scenarios.commitSubject: migrate build from webpack to vite

targetMemories.content: The build uses webpack for bundling.
webpack.config.js defines multiple entry points for the app.

bystanderMemories.content: We host a webinar every month for new engineering hires.
Add web accessibility linting (eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y) to the CI pipeline.

scenarios.description: A commit replacing Jest with Vitest should invalidate the Jest-runner memory, without catching an unrelated word that merely contains 'jest' as a substring.

targetMemories.content: Unit tests are written with jest and run via `npm test`.

bystanderMemories.content: The team celebrated at an end-of-quarter party with jesters and games.

scenarios.description: Deprecating legacyAuth should invalidate the memory describing it, without catching a longer word that contains it as a non-word-boundary substring (naive substring matching's classic failure mode).

targetMemories.content: legacyAuth handles session tokens for old client versions.

bystanderMemories.content: The legacyAuthentication docs are on the wiki archive.

scenarios.description: KNOWN-LIMITATION scenario, included for honesty rather than to flatter either system: removing the 'moment' date library collides with the ordinary English word 'moment'. A word-boundary-aware (or naive substring) matcher cannot tell these apart from the commit subject alone, so the bystander here is expected to fail on both systems unless one does semantic/topic disambiguation.

targetMemories.content: We depend on moment for dates.

bystanderMemories.content: That was a defining moment for the product's roadmap.

scenarios.description: A commit switching state management from Redux to Zustand should invalidate the Redux memory, without catching a compound-word tool name that contains 'Redux' as a non-word-boundary substring (same word-boundary class of test as deprecate-legacyAuth, different verb: 'switch ... from X to Y').
scenarios.commitSubject: switch state management from Redux to Zustand

targetMemories.content: Global UI state is managed with Redux, using slices under src/store/.

bystanderMemories.content: The ReduxDevTools browser extension is still installed for debugging other, unrelated projects.

scenarios.description: A commit converting a widget library from class components to hooks should invalidate memories describing the class-components usage, without catching a memory that mentions the same two words in reversed order ('component classes'), which is not the same phrase the word-boundary matcher looks for.
scenarios.commitSubject: convert legacy widgets from class components to hooks

targetMemories.content: The legacy widget library still uses class components with lifecycle methods.

bystanderMemories.content: Component classes are organized under src/components/, one directory per feature area.

scenarios.description: A commit upgrading the runtime version should invalidate the memory pinning the old version, exercising the 'upgrade ... from X to Y' shape with a multi-word, numeric target (not yet covered by the other commit-message scenarios above).
scenarios.commitSubject: upgrade the runtime from Node 18 to Node 22

targetMemories.content: The runtime is currently pinned to Node 18 in the Dockerfile and CI config.

bystanderMemories.content: An onboarding doc links to a 2019 blog post about why the team originally chose Node over Deno; it does not mention any specific version.

scenarios.description: A commit dropping React should invalidate the memory describing that usage, exercising the 'drop' verb of the remove/drop shape (the existing remove-moment scenario only exercises 'remove'), with a word-boundary bystander sharing 'React' as a non-word-boundary substring. The commit subject is deliberately just 'drop React', not 'drop React from the admin panel' — the remove/drop shape's regex (`/\b(?:remove|drop)\s+(.+?)\s*$/i`) has no 'from'-stripping like the migrate/switch/... shape does, so anything after the target would be captured as part of it too, and the target would then never match the memory body.

targetMemories.content: The admin panel is built with React, using function components and hooks.

bystanderMemories.content: ReactiveX-style Observables power the analytics pipeline, unrelated to the UI framework.

scenarios.description: rAIminiscence-specific v2 mechanism: a memory anchored to a relatedFiles path is staled when git shows that exact file changed after the memory's createdAt, independent of the memory's textual content. The bystander here is anchored to a *different* file that was not touched.

targetMemories.content: webpack.config.js splits vendor and app code into separate bundles for production.

bystanderMemories.content: src/index.ts bootstraps the React app and mounts the router.
